note: Per-lift records. Every property is tagged verified, estimated or unknown. See references/README.md for the photos behind the estimates.

sources.sign: Photo of the information sign in the bottom station: http://rodoaf.remontees-mecaniques.net/usa/timberline/tsd4mag/ok%20(11).JPG
sources.lidar: Oregon DOGAMI lidar canopy height model; USGS 3DEP elevation

lifts.name: Magic Mile

slopeLengthM.note: 5,420 ft on the lift's own sign. Other sources: 1,676 m (rm), 5,500 ft (wiki).

towerCount.note: Single source for the count; 18 are mapped in OpenStreetMap and all 21 line up with lidar returns.

operatingSpeedMps.how: Highest speed reported by a rider reading the lift display (990 ft/min, 2016). Slower speeds of 715 to 850 ft/min are reported in summer.

chairStorage.value: Chairs can be taken off the line and parked in the building beside the bottom station when storms are expected.

uphillSide.how: Read from two photos: riders going up pass to the right of tower 6 (liftblog img_7249); the loading bay is on the east side of the bottom station (liftblog img_7464).

chairSpacingM.how: Derived: 4 seats / (1,600 riders per hour) x 5.0 m/s. Riders describe the spacing as wide.

carrierCount.how: Derived from the loop length and the estimated spacing. Chair numbers 53 and (probably) 74 are visible in photos.

lineGaugeM.how: Typical for a Poma detachable quad of this era; lidar returns from the tower heads spread about 3 m either side of the centre line.

ropeDiameterMm.how: Typical for a detachable quad of this length. Not documented.

stationSpeedMps.how: Typical detachable loading speed. Not documented.

chairDimensions.how: Scaled from photo rm-46 assuming a 2.2 m four-person seat.

towerHeadAboveRopeM.how: Height of the lifting frame above the rope, scaled from photos rm-25 and liftblog img_7249.

stationInteriors.note: Bullwheels, contours and loading areas are not modeled yet.

towerSheaveCounts.note: Only a few towers are documented (4S2C/4S2C, 6S/4S, 6S/6S in rm captions). Counts are currently derived from the rope angle at each tower.

line.note: Centre line from OpenStreetMap way 5282193. s is horizontal distance in meters along this line from its first point.

bottom.note: Building extent from lidar. Rope height and bullwheel position inside are estimates.

top.note: Building extent from lidar. Rope height and bullwheel position inside are estimates.

towers.note: Station exit tower. Position and height from a low lidar return (5.7 m) just outside the building; not in OpenStreetMap. Counted as tower 1 to match the 21 towers reported by remontees-mecaniques.net.
Not in OpenStreetMap. Placed from a lidar peak on the lift line that fits the regular ~100 m tower spacing. Could in principle be a chair caught by the lidar.
Not in OpenStreetMap. Placed from a lidar peak on the lift line that fits the regular ~100 m tower spacing. Could in principle be a chair caught by the lidar.

lifts.towerNote: s and top come from the Oregon DOGAMI lidar canopy height model sampled every 1 m along the line (top = highest return, about +/-1 m). ground comes from USGS 3DEP. Towers marked verified are also mapped in OpenStreetMap within 3 m.
knownMismatches: Stations are still the plain lidar building shells: no open bays, bullwheels, loading area, deck or signs.
Chair parking building beside the bottom station has no rails or doors.
Tower sheave counts are derived, not documented, for most towers.
No tower numbers, chair numbers, ladders cages, wind gauges or catwalks.
No shadows from chairs or towers yet.
Towers are modeled vertical; the real ones lean slightly.
Rope sag is a parabola with an assumed tension, not surveyed.
